title: Browser Architecture
definition: Modern browsers are highly complex, multi-process operating systems. They typically consist of a Browser Process (UI, Network, Storage), multiple Renderer Processes (one per tab, sandboxed), a GPU Process, and Plugin Processes.
simpleExplanation: Chrome runs every tab as a separate mini-program (process) so that if one tab crashes or contains a virus, it doesn't crash your whole computer or steal data from other tabs.
diagramContent:
graph TD
  BP[Browser Process] -->|IPC| RP1[Renderer Process Tab 1]
  BP -->|IPC| RP2[Renderer Process Tab 2]
  BP --> GP[GPU Process]
  BP --> NP[Network Process]
  RP1 --> JS[V8 JS Engine]
  RP1 --> Blink[Blink Render Engine]

answers.question: Define Browser Architecture.
answers.answer: Browser Architecture is a core mechanism in frontend architectures.

answers.question: What is the main bottleneck for Browser Architecture?
answers.answer: Usually network latency or CPU-bound synchronous tasks blocking the main thread.
